title: 5-3-1 Modified for Disc Injury (back injury)
author: Bobby C.
desc: This is for people who can't do squats or traditional deadlifts because of injury or old age or whatever. Obviously, consult your doctor before doing any exercise program.

ex.note: Use a "Z-Press" (seated on floor) if standing hurts.
Use a wide grip; do not lean back excessively.
Keep elbows tucked; chest up.
Strict form; no body swing.
Pull toward forehead; hold for 1s.
Weights held at sides (suitcase style).
Feet high on platform; keep lower back glued to seat.
Slow and controlled.

Hold each "rep" for 10 seconds. Between Reps: No rest. Hold for 10 seconds, "sweep" the floor (touch your hand/knee down for a split second);go right to the next 10-second hold. Between Sets, rest 20.
Actually, Modified Curl-Up: One leg straight, hands under low back. Lift head/shoulders 1" without flattening your back into your hands. Hold 10s. Keep spine neutral.
For the Side Plank, remember that you have two sides—so you’ll do 12 on the left and 12 on the right.
Active Dead Hang: Overhand grip. Pull shoulders down/back. Tuck pelvis slightly. Hold 30-60s. Crucial: Step down onto a box; never drop to the floor to avoid spinal jarring.
Keep feet flat; avoid a high powerlifting arch.
Lay face-down on an incline bench to pull.
Laying on a bench prevents lower back swinging.
Seated on a bench with back support.
Focus on "tucking" the pelvis; no sagging.
Use the high handles. Do not round the spine.
Hold a dumbbell at your chest; it acts as a brace.
Walk tall with heavy dumbbells; don't let them sway.
Keep the neck neutral
